To find the maximum horizontal force that can be applied before the block slips, we need to calculate the **limiting static friction**.

### 1. Identify the Normal Force ($N$)
Since the block is on a horizontal floor and there are no other vertical forces, the normal force is equal to the weight of the block:
$$N = mg$$
$$N = 5 \text{ kg} \times 9.8 \text{ m/s}^2 = 49 \text{ N}$$

### 2. Calculate the Limiting Friction ($f_{s,max}$)
The maximum force of static friction is given by the product of the coefficient of static friction ($\mu_s$) and the normal force:
$$f_{s,max} = \mu_s N$$
$$f_{s,max} = 0.4 \times 49 \text{ N}$$
$$f_{s,max} = 19.6 \text{ N}$$

**Conclusion:**
The maximum horizontal force that can be applied before the block slips is **19.6 N**. Any force greater than this will overcome the static friction and cause the block to accelerate.
